name: etch
description: Preview Europa Universalis IV interface mods while you edit them.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Open a .gui file to see the widgets of its window here.
[Open a .gui File…](command:workbench.action.quickOpen?%5B%22.gui%22%5D)
New to Etch? [Get started](command:etch.getStarted) in six steps.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Etch
walkthroughs.description: Preview your EU4 interface mod beside the code, as the game draws it.

steps.title: Find the game
steps.description:
Etch draws with your game's own sprites, fonts and texts, so it needs the Europa Universalis IV folder. It finds a game installed through Steam by itself, and this step ticks itself once it has. Is your game elsewhere, such as a GOG copy? Set its folder, the one that holds eu4.exe.
[Set the Game Folder](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22etch.gamePath%22%5D)

media.altText: A game folder found through Steam, holding eu4.exe

steps.title: Open your first preview
steps.description:
Open a .gui file of your mod, put the cursor in a window and click **Open Preview** in the editor's title bar. The preview draws that window beside the editor and follows the cursor from window to window.
[Open a .gui File…](command:workbench.action.quickOpen?%5B%22.gui%22%5D)

media.altText: A .gui file in the editor, and the preview of its window beside it

steps.title: Find a widget in the Widget Outline
steps.description:
The **Widget Outline** in the Explorer lists the widgets of the previewed window as a tree. Click one to jump to its line; the buttons on its row hide or show it.
[Show the Widget Outline](command:etch.widgetOutline.focus)

media.altText: The Widget Outline lists the widgets of a window beside the file

steps.title: Fill texts with sample data
steps.description: The game's code writes many texts of a window, such as a province's name. In the preview, **Data ▾** fills them with made-up text, with a save of yours or with what the live game showed.

media.altText: The preview's Data menu and the texts it fills

steps.title: Start the live game (optional)
steps.description:
The live game is EU4 itself beside the editor, with your mod's playset: each file you save goes into it at once, and pick mode jumps from a widget in the game to its line. It needs the Steam version of EU4 1.37.5.
[Start the Live Game](command:etch.startLiveGame)

media.altText: Saving a file reloads it in the live game; a pick goes back to its line

steps.title: Colour your script files
steps.description:
Etch adds no colours to script files, such as .gui, .gfx and event files. Without another extension, VS Code opens them as Plain Text, all in one colour. **CWTools** or **ParadoxCode** colours their keywords, numbers and comments, and you can use either together with Etch. CWTools colours a mod's .txt files only inside a folder named Europa Universalis IV. For a mod kept elsewhere, Etch offers to add a setting so that CWTools colours them too. ParadoxCode is only on the VS Code Marketplace, not on Open VSX. This step ticks itself once one of them is installed.
[Install CWTools](command:workbench.extensions.installExtension?%5B%22tboby.cwtools-vscode%22%5D)
[Install ParadoxCode](command:workbench.extensions.installExtension?%5B%22ParadoxCode.paradoxcode-vscode%22%5D)

media.altText: A script file in one colour as Plain Text, and the same file coloured by CWTools or ParadoxCode

etch.gamePath.markdownDescription: The Europa Universalis IV game folder, the one that holds `eu4.exe`. When empty, Etch finds it through Steam's library list. Etch only reads this folder.

etch.playset.markdownDescription: Mods to preview with, in load order (a later mod's file wins), as mod names or as mod folders or `.mod` descriptors. When not empty it replaces the default playset: the edited mod and the `dependencies` of its descriptor. The edited mod is added last unless the list names it.

etch.language.markdownDescription: The language of the localisation texts that the preview shows in a `.gui` file, and that the editor shows after each localisation key.

etch.editor.completion.markdownDescription: Suggest words as you type in `.gui` files: widget types, keys, sprite names, fonts and values, taken from your playset (the game, your mod and the mods it depends on).

etch.editor.localisationHints.markdownDescription: Show the text of a localisation key, in `#etch.language#`, in grey after the key: in `.gui` files after `text`, `tooltip`, `tooltipText` and `delayedTooltipText`; in the scripts of `events`, `decisions`, `missions` and `common` after `title`, `desc`, `name`, `tooltip` and `custom_tooltip`, and in `common` also after `war_name`, `prov_desc`, `country_desc`, `elector_relation`, `demands_description`, `mercenary_desc_key`, `custom_ai_explanation` and `reform_tooltip`. Ctrl+click a key to open its line in the `.yml` file.

etch.editor.provinceNames.markdownDescription: Show a province's name, in `#etch.language#`, in grey after its id in script files: after `owns = 151`, a `151 = { … }` scope and the other values that Etch: Check Province IDs and Names in the Playset reads as province ids. The name is the playset's localisation key `PROV151`.

etch.editor.rename.markdownDescription: Find All References (Shift+F12) and Rename Symbol (F2) on sprite names: in `.gfx` and `.gui` files and in the script files that name sprites: an event's `picture`, a mission's `icon`, an estate privilege's `icon` and the sprite keys of ten `common` folders (see Hovers and links in Etch's guide). A rename changes only your mod's files. Turn it off if another extension already finds or renames these names: Etch then adds neither, and the other extension's answers stand alone.

enumDescriptions: Where CWTools' EU4 rules cover a sprite, font or `.gui` widget, Etch leaves that answer to CWTools, so it does not show twice.
Etch gives all its answers next to CWTools, so some of them show twice.
etch.cwtools.markdownDescription: What Etch does when CWTools is on too. With `auto`, in files that CWTools reads as EU4, Etch leaves to CWTools what CWTools' EU4 rules cover: Go to Definition on those sprites, their entries and the fonts in the Outline of a `.gfx` file, and the widget types and keys suggested in `.gui` files. Etch's hovers, its sprite and font suggestions and the preview's warnings in the Problems panel stay. With `ignore`, Etch gives all its answers, so some of them show twice.

etch.editor.spriteThumbnails.markdownDescription: Show a small picture of each sprite beside the line numbers, on the lines of a `.gui` file or a script file that name a sprite: an event's `picture`, a mission's `icon` and the other keys listed in Etch's guide under Hovers and links. A strip shows its first frame. Up to 500 pictures per file.

etch.previewResolution.patternErrorMessage: Write default, native or a width × height such as 1920x1080.
etch.previewResolution.markdownDescription: The screen size the preview lays windows out on and evaluates `if_resolution` blocks against: `default` (the resolution in the game's `settings.txt`, else the monitor's), `native` (the monitor's resolution), or a width × height such as `1920x1080`. UI scale is always 1.0. The command **Etch: Choose the Preview Resolution** also offers the corpus resolutions.

etch.liveGame.checkOnSave.markdownDescription: Check an event, decision, mission, scripted effect or scripted trigger file in the live game each time you save it, as **Etch: Check File in the Live Game** does. The game reads the file's triggers and effects but runs none of them. What it finds appears in the Problems panel, with no notice. Needs a running live game with a save loaded; otherwise saving checks nothing.

etch.liveGame.pickModeKey.patternErrorMessage: Write Ctrl or Alt (with Shift if you like) and a letter, a digit or F1-F24, such as Ctrl+Shift+E.
etch.liveGame.pickModeKey.markdownDescription: The key that turns pick mode on and off in the live game: Ctrl or Alt, with Shift if you like, and a letter, a digit or F1-F24. The game binds nothing to the default `Ctrl+Shift+E`; Esc is never taken. A change applies to a running live game at once.
